references.text: God drove the man out and placed cherubim east of the garden of Eden—a parallel to Cain settling east of Eden, even farther from God's presence
Cain was condemned to be a restless wanderer on the earth, which explains his move to the land of Nod (which means 'wandering')
Cain complained that he was driven away from God's face, and in verse 16 we see its fulfillment: he went away from the Lord's presence
After settling in Nod, Cain built a city—the beginning of a civilization outside God's presence
Jonah fled from the Lord's face, a thematic parallel to Cain who went away from the Lord's face
Abel's righteous offering is contrasted with Cain, whose actions led him to leave God's presence
